1.explanation:
• runner-test.js covers how the CLI runner handles and surfaces errors, including formatting and output hooks.  
• lib/i18n/i18n-test.js, locales-test.js, and swap-locale-test.js exercise the core translation functions, locale loading, and swapping logic—crucial for understanding why the error code isn’t run through the translator.  
• index-test.js verifies initialization of the Lighthouse entrypoint (where i18n is wired up) and ensures locale data is loaded before any errors are printed.  
• test-utils.js provides helpers used across multiple tests (mocks, stubs, and setup) that you’ll need to craft a repro scenario or write new tests around this bug.
1.bug_scenario:
When invoking the Lighthouse CLI with an invalid URL (e.g. `node lighthouse-cli www.example.com --view`), the terminal output falls back to showing the raw error identifier and file path instead of a user-friendly, localized message. In the screenshot we see the ChromeLauncher logs, followed by:  

  Runtime error encountered: lighthouse-core/lib/lh-error.js | urlInvalid # 0  
  LLError: INVALID_URL  
  at lighthouse (…/lighthouse-core/index.js:44:11) …  

Rather than using the i18n system to display a translated error message, the CLI is printing the internal error code and path.
